slide.title: A note travels with its element
slide.takeaway: A diagram element may carry a short Markdown note; the model validates it once, and the SVG, the CLI, and the reviewer each read it.

item.label: An optional note on every element
item.description: Element gains an optional note field, in the stored source, the JSON schema, and the published contract.

item.label: Only safe, short Markdown passes
item.description: A note is parsed with the reviewer's own goldmark extensions; only bold, italics, inline code, lists, and http, https, or mailto links pass, in at most 1,000 characters. Blank notes and notes on decorative elements are refused.

item.label: An angle bracket is raw HTML
item.description: Why a note that mentions a tag is refused.
item.body: You might expect <why> to show as text; Markdown parses it as raw HTML, so the note is refused with a hint to write \< or put it in code.

item.label: The SVG carries it as desc
item.description: The renderer adds the note's plain-text projection as the element's desc for screen readers and the standalone SVG. An element without a note renders byte-identically, so the renderer version is unchanged.

item.label: Agents read it without hovering
item.description: diagram describe prints each note under its element and in JSON; diagram get returns it; an update op sets it and null clears it.

item.label: Model and CLI tests
item.description: Validation refusals, the plain-text projection, a golden rendering with notes that strips back to the old bytes, schema bounds, and describe, get, and edit round trips on implementation and review slides.
